title: Observe what happens when main is not static
answer: If the standard `main` method is not declared `static`, the source can still be syntactically valid and may compile, but the normal Java launcher cannot use that instance method as the application entry point. The launcher expects a static entry method so it can begin execution without first creating an object. With a declaration such as `public void main(String[] args)`, launching the class normally results in a runtime launcher error indicating that the main method is not static or that the required main entry point is missing. An instance method named `main` can still be called through an object like any other instance method; it simply does not satisfy the standard application-launch contract.

steps.title: Create a temporary non-static demo
steps.question: To test the launcher rule without damaging the permanent `MainMethodLab` built in earlier lessons, this experiment should live in its own short-lived source file. Why is isolating the non-static example safer than changing the working standard main method and hoping a later lesson restores it?
steps.why: A temporary demo avoids contaminating cumulative permanent state and makes cleanup explicit.
steps.why_te: Non-static main experiment separate temporary file lo unte permanent `MainMethodLab` state safe ga untundi. Working entry point ni break chesi later restore cheyyadam kanna explicit demo/cleanup flow reliable ga untundi.

steps.title: Type a non-static main
steps.question: The method name, visibility, return type, and parameter list can look almost identical to the standard entry point while one missing modifier changes launch behavior completely. What does removing only `static` teach about the launcher's need to invoke main before any object instance exists?
steps.why: The example isolates static as the key difference between a normal launcher entry point and an instance method.
steps.why_te: Ee example lo `public`, `void`, `main`, `String[] args` same ga untayi; `static` matrame remove chestam. Dini valla launcher object create cheyyakunda method invoke cheyyalante static enduku important ani clear ga observe cheyyachu.

steps.title: Inspect the instance method
steps.question: IntelliJ should still recognize `main(String[])` as a valid Java instance method even though it does not satisfy the standalone launch contract. What distinction should the File Structure view help you make between a method being legal Java and a method being a valid launcher entry point?
steps.why: A legal instance method can exist without being the static entry method the Java launcher requires.
steps.why_te: File Structure method ni valid Java member ga chupinchachu, kani valid member undadam standalone launcher entry point avvadam tho same kaadu. Static modifier launch contract lo separate requirement.

steps.title: Compile the non-static class
steps.question: A common misconception is that removing `static` must cause a compile-time syntax error, but Java permits ordinary instance methods named `main`. Why is compiling the file before launching it important for showing that the failure belongs to startup semantics rather than basic source validity?
steps.why: Successful compilation separates legal Java syntax from the Java launcher's entry-point requirements.
steps.why_te: Non-static `main` ordinary instance method ga Java lo legal kabatti compile success avvachu. Compile stage success ayyaka launch stage fail ayithe problem syntax kaadani, entry-point contract ani clear ga telustundi.

steps.title: Launch and observe the error
steps.question: The critical experiment is to ask the normal Java launcher to start a class whose only matching method is an instance method. What should the launcher report when it cannot invoke `public void main(String[] args)` as the required static application entry point?
steps.why: The launcher should reject the class as lacking the required static main entry point.
steps.why_te: Normal launcher `public void main(String[] args)` ni object lekunda invoke cheyyaledu. Kabatti required static main entry point ledu ani runtime launch error report cheyyali.

data.output:
Error: Main method is not static in class NonStaticMainDemo; please define the main method as:
   public static void main(String[] args)

steps.title: Connect the error to JVM startup
steps.question: The compiler accepted the class, but the launcher rejected it because startup occurs before there is any `NonStaticMainDemo` object available for an instance call. How does this result explain the practical reason the recognized Java application entry point is static?
steps.why: Static lets the launcher invoke the method directly from the class without constructing an application object first.
steps.why_te: Launcher start time lo `NonStaticMainDemo` object automatically create cheyyadu. `static` unte class level nundi method direct ga invoke cheyyachu; ee failure exact reason ni runtime behavior tho connect chestundi.

steps.title: Delete the temporary demo
steps.question: This lesson intentionally introduced invalid launcher state only to demonstrate one rule, so allowing the file to survive would pollute later cumulative project replay with an artifact that AeroTopo does not need. Why should the final step explicitly delete the temporary source after the behavior has been proven?
steps.why: Explicit cleanup prevents a temporary learning mutation from becoming accidental permanent project state.
steps.why_te: Demo purpose complete ayyaka temporary `NonStaticMainDemo.java` ni delete cheyyali. Leka pothe later cumulative replay lo unnecessary file permanent state laga survive avvachu; explicit cleanup continuity ni clean ga unchutundi.
